details:
Red Odyssey is an interactive planetary exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Focused on Jezero Crater, one of Mars' most scientifically significant regions, our project aims to make Martian terrain easier to explore, understand, and analyze by combining real orbital imagery, topographic datasets, and geospatial technologies.

The platform features an interactive map with multiple scientific layers, including high-resolution CTX satellite imagery, digital elevation models, contour lines, slope maps, and scientifically relevant locations. These layers allow users to investigate the Martian landscape from different perspectives and better understand its geological and topographic characteristics.

One of Red Odyssey's most innovative features is its terrain-aware route-planning system. Users can select a starting point and destination, while Python-based pathfinding algorithms analyze elevation and slope data to identify potential exploration routes. The system accounts for terrain difficulty, penalizes steeper slopes, and provides useful metrics such as distance and elevation changes.

To develop the project, our team combined several technologies. QGIS was used to process planetary datasets, generate terrain visualizations, and align geographic information. JavaScript, OpenLayers, and Vite power the interactive web experience, while Python and FastAPI handle terrain analysis and route calculations. We primarily relied on scientific datasets provided by USGS Astrogeology and NASA-related resources. We also used AI-assisted development tools, including Codex and ChatGPT, to support programming, research, and technical decisions.

Our creative approach lies in connecting scientific cartography with interactive exploration and algorithmic route planning. Rather than simply displaying a map of Mars, Red Odyssey allows users to investigate how terrain characteristics influence movement and exploration.

Throughout development, we considered data accuracy, coordinate system compatibility, performance, visualization quality, accessibility, and scientific limitations. We designed the platform to communicate terrain information responsibly, recognizing that topographic analysis alone cannot guarantee safe rover navigation.

Ultimately, Red Odyssey aims to make planetary science more accessible and engaging for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts, encouraging curiosity, exploration, and a deeper understanding of the challenges involved in exploring other worlds.
